What's the smallest thing you want to be able to make out — crystals and mining spots inside a cave, individual cave mouths and buildings, whole mountainsides and the trails between them, or the entire range from a distance?
Where does trading happen — a hub with stalls that everyone returns to, a trading post at each cave mouth, or anywhere two players meet, with nothing built for it?
Is the leaderboard a board standing somewhere in the world, or a panel on the screen?

notes_for_us: The prompt self-declares 'adventure' and the loop underneath it is a mining and collection grind, which is Simulation. Both were named, but the shape decision then belonged to neither genre's list — world-underground is Simulation's and Adventure's preset shape had to be swapped out to reach it.

'Some let you see better in the dark' is the only thing in the prompt that specifies lighting, and there is no option, axis or field for how dark an interior is. It went in notes, where the image model will not see it.

Two prompts in this batch asked for a leaderboard and in both the same question came up — wall in the world or panel on screen — with tracker-leaderboard silently assuming the first. The row is defined as a structural wall, so matching a screen leaderboard to it builds a wall nobody asked for.

image_prompt.text: Each player's own factory, entered from the world outside, machines and conveyor lines running inside it
The machines themselves as the entertainment — crushers, cutters, melters, presses and lasers, objects bouncing, rolling and rotating down the conveyors
Walls between factory areas that drop away when bought, from the Starter Factory out to Candy, Toy, Technology, Volcano, Space, Galaxy and Secret
The shop area where upgrades and pet eggs are bought, that every player keeps coming back to
Clear routes from each factory out into the world where objects are collected and back again
The open ground outside the factories where collectable objects appear for the whole server to gather

layout_placement.text: The objects scattered across the map to pick up and carry in — apples and rocks through to meteors and galaxy cores
The RESTART pad at the far end of a maxed factory, trading the factory in for permanent bonuses

mechanics: loop: collect objects, process them, earn money, upgrade, expand, automate, repeat
eight object rarities from Common to Impossible
machine list: crusher, cutter, melter, press, laser, recycler, duplicator, rainbow, galaxy, secret
upgrades: processing speed, machine power, conveyor speed, storage, coin multiplier, crit chance, rare chance, factory size
RESTART prestige for permanent bonuses
pets with six rarities, obtained from eggs, following the player
server-wide events every few minutes: mega object, golden rain, super speed, rainbow, black hole, secret object
a collection book of every object
global leaderboard: richest, highest level, most processed, most secrets, longest playtime
coins flying to the player, damage numbers, glow, sparks, screen shake, combo effects
optimised for mobile, tablet and PC, simple modern UI
notes: Tycoon preset kept for its options but its plot-shared shape swapped for plot-isolated, because each player owns their own factory rather than sharing one

notes_for_us: The conveyor-and-machine line is the entire game and there is no option for it. physics-rig was the only row close enough to take, and it means ragdoll contraptions whose physics are the joke — not an ordered production line whose throughput is the economy. A tycoon's machines are one of the most common things asked for on this platform.

Recurring server-wide events that change the whole map for thirty seconds — golden rain, a black hole — are neither geometry nor mechanics. They are temporary states of the map, and the handoff has one static description with no way to say 'and sometimes this'.

plot-isolated versus a walkable shared world is unresolved by the prompt and changes the entire layout, but the shape had to be committed anyway. The open question is recorded, and the handoff does not mark the shape itself as assumed the way theme and scale are.
